svg.text: FIG 07: 2-PORT BLACK-BOX TERMINAL SYNTHESIS, V-I CHARACTERISTICS & RAPID EXAM CLASSIFIER
Slope-Intercept Parameter Extraction • Terminal Sign Conventions • Multi-Terminal Black Boxes • 60-Second 4-Track Exam Decision Tree

g.text: Any active linear network encapsulated in a closed "black box" with two exposed
terminals A-B possesses an exact linear relationship between terminal voltage V
and load current I_L (current LEAVING terminal A):
• Y-Intercept (I_L = 0 A): Open-Circuit Voltage V_oc = V_th.
• X-Intercept (V = 0 V): Short-Circuit Current I_sc = V_th / R_th = I_N.
• Slope of Characteristic Line: m = dV / dI_L = -R_th ⟹ R_th = -m.
THE 2-PORT SIGN CONVENTION TRAP: I_2 vs. -I_2
The classic GATE 2-Port trap that trips over 75% of candidates:
Standard two-port parameter conventions define port current I₂ as ENTERING Port 2:
Load Current: I_L = -I₂ (Current LEAVING the port)
Terminal Equation in Terms of Port Current I₂:
V₂ = V_th - (-I₂) · R_th = V_th + I₂ · R_th
• If plotting V₂ vs (-I₂): Slope is NEGATIVE (-R_th) and intercept is V_th.
• If plotting V₂ vs (+I₂): Slope is POSITIVE (+R_th) and intercept is V_th.
Check the horizontal axis label! Confusing I₂ with -I₂ flips resistance sign!
GATE PYQ: Parameter Extraction from 2 Points
A linear black-box terminal V₂ vs -I₂ characteristic gives two operating points:
Step 2: Connect Active Load (1 kΩ in series with opposing 10 V):
Extracting V_th and R_th using non-ideal meters:
• Connect resistor R_L1; measure load voltage V_L1.
• Connect resistor R_L2; measure load voltage V_L2.
• Adjust variable load resistor R_L until terminal voltage drops to EXACTLY V_oc / 2.
At that point: R_L ≡ R_th ! (Direct zero-calculation readout!)
When Network 1 (V_th1, R_th1) is connected to Network 2 (V_th2, R_th2):
The two Thévenin equivalents form a single closed loop:
Loop Current Flowing from Network 1 to Network 2:
V_terminal = V_th1 - I_12 · R_th1 = V_th2 + I_12 · R_th2
Load Line Analysis for Non-Linear Elements
When the driving network (V_th, R_th) is connected across a non-linear element
(e.g., diode with non-linear characteristic i_D = f(v_D)):
i_D = (V_th - v_D) / R_th = -v_D / R_th + V_th / R_th
• Plot non-linear device curve: i_D vs v_D.
• Superimpose straight load line with y-intercept I_sc = V_th/R_th and x-intercept V_th.
• The physical operating point Q(V_DQ, I_DQ) is the UNIQUE intersection point!
Thévenin's theorem compresses entire complex linear networks into a single load line!
In multi-stage resistor ladders or cascaded circuits:
3. Shunt branch current: I_shunt = V_out / R_shunt.
4. Prior series current: I_series = I_out + I_shunt (KCL).
5. Work backwards all the way to the input source V_in,calc.
k = V_in,actual / V_in,calc ⟹ True I_out = k · 1 A
Exam Advantage: Solves 6-loop networks with ZERO simultaneous linear equations!
• Two-port matrices can be added if and only if connecting them does not cause
circulating ground loop currents that violate the port condition (I_in = I_out)!
• Ideal 1:1 isolating transformers guarantee valid interconnections.
ONLY Substitution and Tellegen's hold in NON-LINEAR circuits.
Reciprocity and Millman are DESTROYED by dependent sources!
V_s in series with R ⟺ I_s = V_s/R in parallel with R
(Current arrow points towards positive voltage terminal).
VCVS (μ·Vx) in series with R ⟺ VCCS (gm·Vx = μ·Vx/R) in parallel with R
CCVS (r·Ix) in series with R ⟺ CCCS (β·Ix = r·Ix/R) in parallel with R
CRITICAL: Controlling variable (Vx, Ix) must NOT be internal to transformed branch!
Voltmeter: Ideal meter in series with internal multiplier resistance R_v
Ammeter: Ideal meter in parallel with internal shunt resistance R_sh
Source conversions preserve external terminal characteristics identically!
Internal Energy Dissipation is NOT Conserved:
• A Thévenin equivalent dissipates: P_th = I_L² · R_th inside the series resistor.
• A Norton equivalent dissipates: P_N = (I_N - I_L)² · R_th inside the shunt resistor.
Thévenin dissipates ZERO power: P_th = 0 W
Norton dissipates FULL power: P_N = I_N² · R_th ≠ 0 W !
Thevenin and Norton equivalents are strictly TERMINAL EQUIVALENTS.
Do NOT calculate internal network efficiency using the equivalent model!
Original circuit internal power must always be computed from original branch currents.
Multiple independent sources, asking for individual source contributions
→ SUPERPOSITION THEOREM (Keep dependent sources active; P ≠ P₁+P₂!)
TRACK B: Load Resistance Variation / Terminal Output
Target response in single load R_L; multiple values of R_L to evaluate
→ THÉVENIN / NORTON (Case 1: R_eq; Case 2: Voc/Isc; Case 3: 1V Test Source)
Find load parameter for maximum power transfer
→ MPTT (DC: R_L=R_th; AC 7-Cases: Z_L=Z_th*; Trap: If internal R var → R=0!)
TRACK D: Swapped Sources / Parallel Buses / Black-Box
Source/meter positions interchanged, or parallel source branches
"Classify the track first. Pick the highest-leverage shortcut. Finish in under 60 seconds."
Never guess equations — let topological constraints guide your pen.
THE 5 GOLDEN COMMANDMENTS OF NETWORK THEOREMS
In Superposition, Thevenin, and Norton, controlled sources stay active ALWAYS!
P_tot ≠ P₁ + P₂ unless frequencies are mutually orthogonal!
If internal source resistor is variable, set R_s = 0 Ω, NOT R_s = R_L!
4. AC Load Power is Active Power (Watts):
P_L = |I_L|² · R_L. Pure reactances consume 0 W average active power.
5. Use the 30-Second T-Network Shortcut for Reciprocity:
Extract R_a, R_b, R_c from test states and solve target loads in 2 simple KVL lines!
Master these 5 rules to guarantee zero negative marks in GATE 2027!
• Modules 1–3 contain every theorem tested in GATE Network Theory over 35 years.
• Source deactivation gives the reference frame for all equivalent resistance values.
• Thévenin and Norton 3 cases cover all passive, active, and controlled source circuits.
• MPTT gives the theoretical power and efficiency limits of electrical engineering.
• Reciprocity and Millman provide high-speed analytical shortcuts for complex networks.
• Substitution, Compensation, and Tellegen establish deep topological conservation.
• Black-box linear parameter extraction connects theory to experimental reality.
Prepared for IISc Bengaluru & IIT GATE examination standards.
